problem: The sentence 'Two resistors set the whole Q-point' is misleading. Because the gate current is zero, R_G carries no DC current and has no effect on the DC operating point; only R_D and the device parameters set it. A student may believe changing R_G shifts the Q-point.
fix: Say: 'R_D and the device set the Q-point; R_G only closes the feedback path (its value affects AC input resistance, not the DC bias).'

problem: K_n is called the transconductance parameter, but many textbooks write the same law as I_D = ½ k_n (V_GS − V_TN)² with k_n = μ_n C_ox (W/L). A student moving between books will use the wrong factor of ½.
fix: Add: 'Some books write I_D = ½ k_n (V_GS − V_TN)², where k_n = μ_n C_ox (W/L); here K_n already contains that ½, so K_n = ½ k_n.'

problem: The saturation condition is given only 'for a JFET' and 'for an enhancement MOSFET'. The n-channel depletion MOSFET, discussed in this same section, uses the same condition with V_P and is left out, so the student may think it follows a different rule.
fix: Write: 'V_DS > V_GS − V_P for a JFET or depletion MOSFET, and V_DS > V_GS − V_TN for an enhancement MOSFET.'

problem: The trap mixes two ideas: it says R1 and R2 carry no gate current, then mentions R_G may be 1 MΩ. R_G is not part of the divider, so the last clause reads as if it explains the divider.
fix: Split it: 'R1 and R2 carry no gate current, so they form an unloaded divider and V_G = V_DD R2/(R1 + R2). R_G only ties the gate to the divider node and may be 1 MΩ or more.'
